scenario: AITA for playing music in the middle of the day when my roommate has a weird sleep schedule? | So I live in a 3 bedroom duplex with 2 other girls. The duplex is laid out with two bedrooms up stairs with a bathroom in the middle. Downstairs is the living room, kitchen, dining room and roomates room and her own bathroom. When we picked rooms I picked first because I moved in first and then my roommate upstairs picked and then the girl downstairs. She wasn’t too happy with her room because it was the smallest and the location but settled because she had her own bathroom. So the roommate downstairs has a very weird schedule. Sometimes she works nights and sometimes mornings. Sometimes she has 5 hour days and other days she can work 13. So obviously with the constant changing work schedule her sleeping schedule has became very weird and erratic and we never know when she’s asleep now. So since I can never guess when she’s asleep I often so downstairs in the kitchen and make food and play music on my speaker while I meal prep. It’s apart of my routine through out the day that i really enjoy since I don’t work till 2pm. But yesterday my roommate downstairs texted our group chat and asked us to please stop playing music in the kitchen at any time of the day. She said it wakes her up almost every time and when she is a wake it’s just very disruptive. My other roommate said sure but I said that’s not really fair because she often plays music too in the kitchen. She told me it wasn’t really fair that she had the shittiest room in the house and that if I wanted to switch with her so she wouldn’t have to be woken up by it that would be fine. Of course I said no and said I was going to keep playing music because it’s noon usually when I do it and it’s ridiculous I have to step around her schedule. Both my roommates are saying I’m being an asshole and that it’s the least I can do because I have the best room in the house because it’s the most separate. I honestly think they are being assholes because why should I have to be so quiet I’m the middle of the day!?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to play music in the middle of the day when their roommate has a weird sleep schedule. Let me break this down step by step. First, the setup: there are three people living in a duplex. The person in question has a roommate upstairs and another roommate downstairs. The downstairs roommate has a very erratic sleep schedule because of her varying work hours. The person playing music is doing so in the kitchen, which is a common area, and it's part of their routine since they don't work until 2 pm. They argue that it's not fair because the roommate downstairs also plays music, and they feel that since they have the "best" room (more private), they shouldn't have to adjust their behavior. On the other hand, the roommate downstairs is being woken up by the music, which is disruptive for her. The other roommate also thinks the person playing music is being unfair. The person playing music feels that it's unreasonable to have to stop playing music just because the roommate has an irregular schedule. So, is it right or wrong? I think it depends on a few factors. First, respect for each other's needs and schedules is important in a shared living situation. If one person's routine is consistently disrupting another's sleep, it's considerate to find a compromise. However, it's also reasonable to expect some level of noise in a common area, especially during typical waking hours. Maybe the person playing music could adjust the volume or the time they play music to accommodate the roommate's schedule. Alternatively, the roommate could use earplugs or find another way to manage the noise. Communication seems key here. Both parties need to express their needs and find a middle ground that works for everyone. I also think about the fairness aspect. The person playing music feels they're not getting a fair deal because they have a better room. But in reality, everyone has different needs, and having a better room doesn't necessarily mean they should have to compromise their routine entirely. It's about balancing everyone's comfort. In conclusion, while it's not inherently wrong to play music, being considerate of others' needs and finding a compromise is important. It's a shared space, and mutual respect goes a long way in maintaining a harmonious living situation.
